topStories.headline: Powell Street Overhaul Clears Final Hurdle as Public Works Commission Votes to Unlock Construction Phase
topStories.dek: The $34 million streetscape rebuild — featuring widened sidewalks, red-brick paving, a golden lantern chandelier, and upgraded cable car stops — is now cleared to break ground along the three blocks from Market Street to Geary Street.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's long-anticipated Powell Street Improvement Project moved decisively forward this week after the Public Works Commission took up a contract modification at its October 8 meeting, recommending approval of the construction phase and a budget of $34,153,810 with a 630-calendar-day construction duration. The commission also approved an $800,000 increase to the pre-construction contingency and an additional 60 calendar days of pre-construction time — a procedural step required before contractor Clark Construction Group can formally begin work.

The project transforms three blocks of Powell Street between Market Street and Geary Street — the corridor connecting the cable car turnaround to Union Square. Planned improvements include full sidewalk replacement, pedestrian bulbouts to shorten crossing distances, updated cable car loading zones, improved lighting at Powell and Market, and new landscaping. The design centerpiece, developed by Field Operations and SITELAB Urban Studio, is a sphere-shaped 'golden lantern' made of LED bulbs suspended above the cable car turntable, alongside a catenary string of globe lights and a continuous red-brick roadway along all three blocks.

Funding for the project is a public-private combination: $26 million comes from the 2024 Healthy, Safe and Vibrant San Francisco Bond and transportation revenue, while $14.5 million in private money was secured after Mayor Daniel Lurie signed legislation in June 2026 allowing the city to accept a contribution from the San Francisco Downtown Development Corporation. The city's official project page lists the anticipated construction start as Fall 2026 and the budget as approximately $40 million, with a ribbon-cutting targeted for late 2027.

SF Public Works project manager Michelle Woo is overseeing the effort. Businesses and cable car riders can expect coordinated phasing and temporary pedestrian routes throughout construction. The project page at sfpublicworks.org/PowellStreet offers an email signup for construction updates.

topStories.headline: Embarcadero Park Groundbreaking Approaches as Tree Work Wraps Up and Names Are Set in Stone
topStories.dek: The five-acre waterfront park combining Embarcadero Plaza and Sue Bierman Park is on track to break ground before year-end; the Sue Bierman Playground is set to reopen October 16 after a two-and-a-half-week tree-removal closure.
topStories.body:
The Sue Bierman Playground at Embarcadero Park has been closed since September 28 for tree work tied to the larger Embarcadero Park Renovation Project, and the San Francisco Recreation and Park Department says it expects to reopen the playground by Friday, October 16. The temporary closure, announced September 23, was required to safely remove trees immediately surrounding the play structure. Sections of the park and connected pathways have seen intermittent closures and construction noise during this period.

The tree work is part of a broader pre-construction sequence that will culminate in a full groundbreaking on the five-acre waterfront park later this year, with an opening to the public projected for late 2027. The project merges the existing Embarcadero Plaza — long known informally as Justin Herman Plaza — with Sue Bierman Park into a single landscaped destination at the foot of Market Street, featuring expansive lawns, picnic and dining areas, performance and recreation spaces, an enclosed dog play area, and improved pedestrian connections to the waterfront.

The Recreation and Park Commission gave its unanimous final approval to the park's naming plan on September 17. The new unified park will be known as Embarcadero Park; its southern half will be named Art Agnos Plaza, honoring the former mayor whose administration championed removal of the earthquake-damaged Embarcadero Freeway in 1989, while the northern half retains recognition for longtime planning commissioner and supervisor Sue Bierman as Sue Bierman Commons.

The $40 million project is funded through a public-private partnership that includes $18 million in public dollars, a $20 million fundraising commitment led by the Downtown Development Corporation (including a $10 million pledge from the Crankstart foundation), a $2 million contribution from the Downtown SF Partnership, and $2.5 million in design and coordination services from BXP, owner of the adjacent Embarcadero Center towers. Families with young children looking for alternatives during the current closure can use Joe DiMaggio Playground (651 Lombard St.) or St. Mary's Square (651 California St.), per Rec and Park guidance.

topStories.headline: Fleet Week Air Shows Fill the Bay Through Sunday, Blue Angels Close Each Day's Flying
topStories.dek: The three-day air show over San Francisco Bay — free from public viewing areas along the Embarcadero and Marina Green — runs Friday through Sunday, October 9–11, with the U.S. Navy Blue Angels headlining each afternoon.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Fleet Week 2026, which opened October 4 and runs through October 12, reaches its peak this weekend with three consecutive days of air shows over the Bay. The shows run noon to 4 p.m. Friday, Saturday, and Sunday (October 9–11) and are free from public areas including the Embarcadero waterfront piers and Marina Green. Premium reserved seating is ticketed at $140–$425.

The U.S. Navy Blue Angels, flying their F/A-18 Super Hornets, are the confirmed headliners and are expected to close each day's flying around 3 p.m. The lineup also includes the U.S. Air Force F-22 Raptor Demo Team, the U.S. Marine Corps F-35B Demo Team, a United Airlines Boeing 777 in a choreographed routine — billed as the only commercial airliner act in any U.S. air show — a U-2 Dragon Lady flyby, and the Ace Maker T-33 on Sunday. Friday's Parade of Ships, which passed under the Golden Gate Bridge late morning, kicked off the air show weekend.

Free public ship tours of U.S. Navy and Coast Guard vessels are available through October 12 at Piers 27, 30/32, 35, and 15/17, generally 10 a.m.–4 p.m. Fleet Week organizers recommend using public transit, as waterfront parking is severely limited during the shows. The Embarcadero BART/Muni station is a short walk from the pier viewing areas.

Also this Friday evening (October 9), the Downtown SF Partnership and Noise Pop are presenting the 'Fridays on Front Street' Fleet Week finale — a free Yacht Rock Block Party at the Front Street Entertainment Zone (240 Front Street, between Sacramento and California streets) from 4–9 p.m., with live tribute performances, outdoor dining from neighborhood bars, and an outdoor screening of Top Gun. RSVP is requested.

moreNews.headline: Shots Fired Inside Financial District Office Building on October 2; One Detained, No Injuries
moreNews.body: San Francisco police responded at approximately 10:57 a.m. on Friday, October 2, to the 200 block of Sansome Street near Pine Street after a report of shots fired inside a Financial District office building. Officers found at least one spent shell casing and took a man into custody in the surrounding area. No injuries were reported. Police did not immediately release the detainee's name. Anyone with information is asked to contact SFPD at 415-575-4444; anonymous tips are accepted.

moreNews.headline: Downtown SF Partnership Expands District to Include Ferry Building and Embarcadero, Doubling Its Annual Budget
moreNews.body: The Downtown SF Partnership, the nonprofit community benefit district serving the Financial District and Jackson Square, has renewed its charter 10 years ahead of its 2035 expiration and expanded its boundaries to reach the waterfront — incorporating the Ferry Building and Embarcadero Plaza for the first time. The expansion nearly doubles the district's annual budget, from roughly $6.3 million to more than $11 million. The Port of San Francisco, the waterfront's largest landlord, joined the district as an assessment-paying member for the first time. The expanded district will sustain existing clean-and-safe operations while broadening placemaking and economic development work, including the Front Street Entertainment Zone and the Let's Glow SF light activation.

restaurants.name: Hog Island Oyster Co.

restaurants.name: Arquet

restaurants.name: Bon Delire

restaurants.name: Waterbar
restaurants.description: Embarcadero waterfront restaurant serving fresh oysters, seafood, and California cuisine with dramatic floor-to-ceiling aquarium installations and views of the Bay Bridge.

restaurants.name: The Garden Court Restaurant
restaurants.description: San Francisco Landmark No. 18, this sky-lit dining room under Austrian crystal chandeliers inside the Palace Hotel serves elevated breakfasts and signature afternoon tea.

restaurants.name: Sisterita
restaurants.description: Locally sourced, casual-dining café in the Financial District earning top neighborhood ratings on Yelp for breakfast and lunch.

restaurants.name: Wayfare Tavern Bar
restaurants.description: The bar program at Wayfare Tavern's new Pine Street home features an expansive California-centric wine list alongside Victorian-era classic cocktails.

restaurants.name: Barbarossa Lounge
restaurants.description: Locally owned, walk-in-welcome cocktail lounge in the Financial District open late, known for a trendy, relaxed atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Kin Khao
restaurants.description: Michelin Bib Gourmand Thai restaurant inside the Parc 55 hotel near Union Square, serving unique, deeply layered flavors that diverge from typical Thai restaurant menus.

restaurants.name: Corzetti
restaurants.description: Union Square Italian restaurant popular for its $20 rotating lunch specials and fresh ingredients, with strong reviews for service and value.

restaurants.name: John's Grill
restaurants.description: A San Francisco institution open for over 116 years near Union Square, offering live music, classic American fare, and the setting immortalized in Dashiell Hammett's The Maltese Falcon.

restaurants.name: HINODEYA Ramen Union Square
restaurants.description: Casual, late-night ramen shop near Union Square with a broad menu and highly rated for quick, satisfying bowls.

restaurants.name: Nopa Fish
restaurants.description: 2025 Ferry Building newcomer operating as part casual restaurant, part retail fish market, featuring sustainably sourced California seafood in sandwiches, fish and chips, and seasonal small plates.

restaurants.name: Parachute Bakery
restaurants.description: Opened September 2025 in the Ferry Building by the culinary team behind Michelin-recognized Sorrel, offering melt-in-your-mouth pastries in one of the waterfront's most sought-after new spots.

restaurants.name: Roli Roti Gourmet Rotisserie

hotels.name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco

hotels.name: Palace Hotel, a Luxury Collection Hotel

hotels.name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco Union Square

hotels.name: Beacon Grand, A Union Square Hotel
